posts.name: LLMScout
posts.tagline: Check if LLMs can cite your site.
posts.description: As AI-Overview CTRs plummet from 7.3% to 1.6% (Ahrefs, Dec 2025), LLMScout helps ensure your site remains visible. This cross-platform, MIT-licensed CLI runs 21 checks to verify if 7 major AI bots can find, parse, and cite your content. It is ultra-lightweight, has no runtime dependencies in Python and just two in TypeScript (cheerio, commander). Use "Fleet mode" to audit entire client rosters in one command. It is 100% free with no accounts or paid tiers.

posts.name: WebDAV Browser - iOS App
posts.tagline: Scan and back up documents to your own server
posts.description: I fly a drone and keep the 4K footage on a Hetzner Storage Box. No iOS app could just play it — they all download almost the whole file first, then stutter. So I built one with real streaming. The rest I added because I needed it. Search that works on-device. Offline files. A scanner, because letters arrive every day and I'd rather they land on my own server than in someone else's cloud.

posts.name: SeeBoop
posts.tagline: A pet cam that tells you the truth when it's offline
posts.description: Every pet monitor listens for "noise." SeeBoop's AI runs on the device itself and tells barks, meows, and crashes apart, so the alert says what actually happened. Any spare phone, tablet, or laptop becomes the camera; a QR scan pairs it. Video is peer-to-peer and end-to-end encrypted, so our servers never see a frame. Live monitoring is free forever: no ads, no trial, no card. And when the connection drops, it says so instead of showing you a frozen frame.
